To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
APS and SPPS coatings show better resistance to hot corrosion than conventional YSZ coating.
The state of the Art YSZ coating was found to completely delaminated within 120 h in molten NaSO4 V2 O 5 environment by forming yttria vanadate and m zirconia.
The hot corrosion behaviour of Gd LC coatings is better than that of the state of the art YSZ in molten Na 2SO4 V 2O 5 (1: 1) at 900 deg. C
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of Gd LC based double layered coatings by APS and SPPS techniques and their comparative performance evaluation with respect to YSZ based double layered coatings in molten Na V environment.
the development of Gd LC based thermal barrier coatings for advanced gas turbine applications.
the development of a new generation of thermal barrier coating system based on Gd-doped ceria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the SPPS GDC coating was found to have the highest hot corrosion resistance among the coatings investigated.
the Gd LC coating is a promising candidate to replace YSZ as a thermal barrier coating material in the future.
the SPPS G d LC coatings are found to be more susceptible to molten salt attack than APS G d LC coatings.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the APS technique can be employed for developing double layered Gd LC coatings for high temperature applications, whereas, SPPS technique may be used for developing single layered coatings.
, the Gd LC coatings are more prone to hot corrosion than the YSZ and APS Gd LC coatings.
, SPPS GDL C coatings were found to have better adherence with bondcoat and were more resistant to densification compared to APS Gd LC coatings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPPS technique can be used for depositing Gd LC coatings with improved adherence with bond coat and also, withstanding the molten salt attack for longer duration.
the Gd LC coating developed by conventional APS process has better hot corrosion resistance than SPPS G d Lc coatings in sulfate and sulfate-vanadate environments.
SPPS technique can be employed for developing high performance thermal barrier coatings with enhanced corrosion and oxidation resistance.
